newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus welcomes Eurocourt ruling against Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus welcomes Eurocourt ruling against Turkey.

text.p: Cyprus on Wednesday welcomed a ruling of the European Court of Human Rights that Turkey had violated the right to property of a Greek Cypriot woman who lost access to her land in northern Cyprus when Turkish troops invaded in 1974.
"It is a great sucess," Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides told reporters.

In a widely-watched case expected to set a precedent, the Strasbourg Court dismissed Turkey's argument that the European human rights convention did not apply to its occupation of the northern half of the Mediterranean island since it occurred before Ankara accepted its jurisdiction.
"I believe its effects can be enormous," said Clerides. "If we take into account those who were forced to leave their homes then the effects can be greater."

Some 200,000 Greek Cypriots were displaced in the Turkish invasion of the northern third of the island in 1974 sparked by a brief coup engineered by the military regime in power in Greece at the time.
The Court ruled by 11 votes to six that Turkey nad violated Titina Loizidou's property rights by denying her access to plots of land in Kyrenia, northern Cyprus.
It gave Turkey six months to submit observations on Loizidou's claim for compensation.

But it dismissed her claim that she had lost her home, noting that she had not been living in Kyrenia at the time and that her intention to live in one of the flats she had been building in northern Cyprus "strained the meaning of the notion "home"."
